Links: it names itself and its vocabulary

# GET http://gateway/repos/JogoShugh/heart-github-test/pulls/2325
# Accept: application/hal+json
number: 2325
title: "Renewals: none during the audit"
state: open
mergeable_state: clean
_links:
  self:
    href: /repos/JogoShugh/heart-github-test/pulls/2325
  curies:
    - name: scm
      href: /profiles/scm#{rel}
      templated: true
  alternate:
    href: https://github.com/JogoShugh/heart-github-test/pull/2325
    type: text/html
  scm:commits:
    href: /repos/JogoShugh/heart-github-test/pulls/2325/commits
  scm:diff:
    href: https://github.com/JogoShugh/heart-github-test/pull/2325.diff
    type: text/x-diff

Where it is, and what its words mean

  • self: its own address, handed over, never built.
  • curies: scm: names resolve to one shared vocabulary, for both forges.
  • alternate: the forge’s own page, for people.
  • Typed links: GitHub’s *_url members became links and left the data.
say: The gateway's answer adds HAL links: self, the scm: curie that says where the relation names are defined, the forge's own page as an alternate, and typed links to related resources. GitHub's own *_url members became these links and left the data.

deck:ref.name: rule-4
deck:ref.label: Rule 4 · No fixed URIs
deck:ref.title: No fixed resource names or hierarchies
deck:ref.summary: In brief: the server owns its namespace and tells the client how to build addresses: forms, URI templates.
deck:ref.quote: “A REST API must not define fixed resource names or hierarchies (an obvious coupling of client and server). Servers must have the freedom to control their own namespace. Instead, allow servers to instruct clients on how to construct appropriate URIs, such as is done in HTML forms and URI templates, by defining those instructions within media types and link relations. [Failure here implies that clients are assuming a resource structure due to out-of band information, such as a domain-specific standard, which is the data-oriented equivalent to RPC’s functional coupling].”
deck:ref.cite: Roy T. Fielding, “REST APIs must be hypertext-driven”
